guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul / Schon signature models (Paul Reed Smith / Gibson)
guitar.evidence: Neal Schon is well known for Gibson Les Pauls and later his own PRS/Gibson signature models.

tone.target: bright 80s arena lead with delay and chorus sheen
tone.profile: bright 80s arena lead with delay and chorus sheen
tone.summary: A clean/crunch foundation built around the UK 45 or UK SLP, enhanced with Chorus for sheen, Digital Delay for space, and a touch of EQ to emphasize upper mids.
corrections: keep the lead glossy, not gritty
avoid tube-screamer crunch as main flavor

rig.name: Journey - Don't Stop Believin' - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Slightly boost signal level for consistency and polish.
Provide a smooth, non-aggressive crunch foundation (like JCM/Marshall clean edge).
blocks.gap: The Green OD is chosen over Blues OD for its slightly more open and less aggressive breakup character, fitting the 'glossy' requirement.

alternatives.reason: Could also work but might be too gritty.

blocks.purpose: Add the required 80s modulation sheen and width.
Simulate the bright, articulate British tone (JCM-style) without heavy crunch.
blocks.gap: The UK SLP is ideal for polished 80s lead tones. We avoid the full power of the UK 45/UK 50 to keep it glossy and less aggressive.

alternatives.reason: Might be too raw or punchy.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British 4x12 voicing required for arena rock.
Boost the upper mids and high frequencies to achieve 'bright' and 'polished 80s' sheen.
Add the required short delay and sense of space/polish.
Add subtle room ambience to glue the sound and enhance the 'arena' feel.
blocks.gap: Plate reverb might be too metallic; Room provides a natural, polished sheen.

alternatives.reason: Could work but risks sounding overly bright or artificial.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR to better capture polished 80s arena sheen and upper-mid articulation.

proposals.reason: Enhance the polished, bright '80s sheen and upper-mid articulation.
